Personality: Tulag is an exceedingly realistic and aloof lord. As the head of Clan Arkit, he has little interest in chasing hollow heroic fame across the steppe; on the contrary, his excessive caution in war has led some to whisper privately that he lacks nerve. Decidedly tight-fisted in the distribution of resources, he prefers careful financial stewardship to preserve his family's wealth over generous rewards. Displaying neither excessive mercy nor a taste for underhanded plotting, his measured, detached manner makes him difficult to read. In his view, emotion is a sign of weakness, and only secure fiefs and the continuation of his lineage are worth his attention. Handling state affairs with near-mechanical composure, he maintains the posture of a cool observer in the power struggles of the Khuzait Khanate, neither giving his heart lightly nor engaging in blind opportunism.
Background: Tulag inherited the foundations laid by his father Kuyug to become the leader of the prominent Khuzait house of Arkit. Holding court in the prosperous city of Ortongard and governing the strategic stronghold of Usek Castle, he is a figure of immense influence within the realm. Although he possesses accomplished mounted martial arts and well-rounded combat skills, he prefers to rely on stout fortifications to guard his clan's interests rather than court risk upon the open steppe. Under Monchug Khan's reign, while he maintains nominal fealty, he knows well the ambitions and grievancesvarious tribes harbor toward the throne. Placing his family's future in his children Kada, Temun, and Abagai, he is dedicated to preserving the foundations of Clan Arkit amid turbulent Khanate politics, watching every stirring across the steppe with a cold gaze as the order established by Urkhun begins to loosen.
